modes.sha224: CTRL.MODE=0, 224-bit truncated digest (first 7 words), NIST init 0xc1059ed8..

notes.function: NIST FIPS-180-4 SHA-256 + SHA-224 dual-mode hash accelerator. 512-bit padded message block per L2/L4 (padding done by SW). Memory-mapped register-file interface per L3/L5: cs/we/address[7:0]/write_data[31:0] -> read_data[31:0]/error.
notes.microarchitecture: Iterative single-cycle round. 64 compression rounds + 1 load + 1 finalize = 66 cycles per 512-bit block (matches L1/L2/L7 reference latency). Message schedule W[0..63] is computed on-the-fly with a 16-deep shift-register sliding window (sha256_core) per FIPS-180-4 sec 6.2.2. K[0..63] round constants in a combinational ROM (sha256_k) transcribed from FIPS-180-4 sec 4.2.2. Round datapath uses a CARRY-SAVE-ADDER (3:2 compressor) tree to reduce the multi-operand T1/T2 sums (e'=d+h+Sigma1+Ch+K+W; a'=+Sigma0+Maj) to redundant (sum,carry) form, collapsed by a single CARRY-SELECT final adder per result. This replaces the ~6-deep sequential ripple-carry chain with a CSA tree + one 16-bit-ripple carry-select CPA, closing setup at the cold ss_n40C_1v60 corner. Latency UNCHANGED (still one round/clock, 66 cycles/block); arithmetic is bit-exact mod 2^32 (NIST KAT + secworks co-sim verified).
notes.mode_handling: SHA-256 and SHA-224 share an identical round function; they differ only in the 8 initial hash values (FIPS-180-4 sec 5.3.2/5.3.3). MODE selects the init constants at INIT time. SHA-224 truncation (drop H7) is applied implicitly on the digest read side (SW reads DIGEST0..6).
notes.block_word_order: BLOCK0 (addr 0x10) is the most-significant 32-bit word of the 512-bit block => W[0]. Big-endian word packing, matching NIST message-block convention.
notes.timing_contract: Synchronous, active-LOW reset clears FSM to idle and sets STATUS.READY=1. SW writes BLOCK0..15, writes CTRL with MODE+INIT (or NEXT), polls STATUS.READY, then reads DIGEST0..7. Core only launches a new hash from idle (in-flight commands ignored, satisfying L7 'INIT during BUSY' corner).
notes.io_delay: default per L9.1.3 (20% of clock period); no SDC override.
notes.verification: Validated bit-exact vs NIST FIPS-180-4 known-answer vectors (SHA-256 'abc', empty, 2-block; SHA-224 'abc') by iverilog functional sim, and cross-checked vs upstream secworks reference RTL at VERIFY stage only (oracle, not input).
